---
title: Inputs and outputs
description: Which columns polars-umap accepts, and how to work with the embedding it returns.
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
vectors = rng.normal(size=(200, 8)).astype(np.float32)
```

## Input

polars-umap accepts two kinds of input.

### One vector per row

A single `Array` or `List` column, where each row holds one vector. This is the natural shape for
embeddings from a language or image model.

```{python}
import polars_umap as pu

df = pl.DataFrame({"embedding": vectors})  # Array(Float32, 8)
df.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(random_state=0)).head(3)
```

A `List` column works too, as long as every row has the same length:

```{python}
as_list = df.with_columns(pl.col("embedding").arr.to_list())
as_list.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(random_state=0)).head(3)
```

Lists of different lengths raise an error, because UMAP needs every vector to have the same
dimensionality.

### Several numeric columns

Pass several numeric columns to `pu.umap()` and they're stacked into a feature matrix, like `X` in
scikit-learn:

```{python}
wide = pl.DataFrame(vectors, schema=[f"feature_{i}" for i in range(8)])
wide.select(pu.umap("feature_0", "feature_1", "feature_2", random_state=0)).head(3)
```

Selectors and regular expressions work too:

```{python}
import polars.selectors as cs

wide.select(
    pu.umap(cs.starts_with("feature_"), random_state=0).alias("from_selector"),
    pu.umap(pl.col("^feature_.*$"), random_state=0).alias("from_regex"),
).head(3)
```

### Data types

Integer, float and boolean values are all converted to `Float32`, which is what the UMAP
implementation uses internally. `Float64` input gives the same result as `Float32` input.

## Output

Expressions return an `Array(Float32, n_components)` column with one point per input row, in the
same order. The column is named after the first input column; use `.alias()` to rename it.

```{python}
out = df.select(xyz=pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(n_components=3, random_state=0))
out.schema
```

To get one column per component, use `.arr.get()`, `.arr.to_struct()` or the DataFrame helper:

```{python}
out.select(
    pl.col("xyz").arr.get(0).alias("x"),
    pl.col("xyz").arr.get(1).alias("y"),
    pl.col("xyz").arr.get(2).alias("z"),
).head(3)
```

```{python}
df.umap.fit_transform("embedding", n_components=3, random_state=0).head(3)
```

The helper takes `output="array"` to add a single Array column instead, `name=` to name that
column, and `prefix=` to change the `umap_` prefix of the component columns.

## Small inputs

UMAP needs a few points to do anything meaningful. polars-umap handles tiny inputs gracefully,
which matters when you run it per group:

- 0 rows give an empty result;
- 1 row is placed at the origin;
- 2 rows are placed one unit apart;
- otherwise, `n_neighbors` is reduced to the number of rows minus one when needed, as umap-learn
  does.
